capex_override.ack_reason: Out-of-band by construction: the engine has NO filed capex value to band against (last_filed_value is null) because Regency tags its capital spending as PaymentsToDevelopRealEstateAssets, outside the engine's candidate tag list. The value is not an estimate — it is the FY2025 figure printed in the FY2025 10-K's cash flow statement and MD&A, verified directly in the filing document.
capex_override.reason: DATA_GAP:capex — capex missing for FY2023, 2024, 2025 of the last 3 (in fact all years under engine candidate tags). The override value is the LATEST filed year's (FY2025) development-and-capital-improvements spend, because the final base is the TTM pin: ttm.py fills every capex leg with this override (no filed leg exists under its candidate tags), so the pin is only honest at the current spend level — at FY2025's $435,112 thousand the TTM pin is $2.00/share vs a true TTM of $1.98/share computed from filed 10-Q YTD development spend (FY2025 $435,112 − Q1 2025 $101,386 + Q1 2026 $105,071 = $438,797 thousand TTM spend; analysis.md), while at FY2024's $343,368 thousand the pin would read $2.50/share on a capex leg the filings contradict (spend has plateaued at the FY2025 level: Q1 2026 $105,071 thousand vs Q1 2025 $101,386 thousand). Cost of the choice, disclosed: the engine applies the one value to every gap year, so the normalized 3-yr median reads ~$1.82/share — below every filed year — an artifact; the true per-year median at each year's filed spend and filed diluted share count is $2.31/share and the true latest-FY figure is $2.05/share (analysis.md method range). Acquisitions of operating real estate ($104,153 thousand in 2025, $45,405 thousand in 2024, same statements) are excluded, consistent with the engine's convention of excluding PaymentsToAcquireBusinesses from capex for non-REIT filers.
capex_override.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-13), consolidated statements of cash flows and MD&A Summary of Cash Flow Activity: 'Real estate development and capital improvements' $435,112 thousand in 2025 and $343,368 thousand in 2024; the 2023 figure $232,855 thousand is the same line as tagged PaymentsToDevelopRealEstateAssets in EDGAR companyfacts (10-Q YTD facts of the same tag give Q1 2025 $101,386 thousand and Q1 2026 $105,071 thousand). Regency files no PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment or any other engine candidate capex tag in any year — its capital spending is tagged PaymentsToDevelopRealEstateAssets, which the engine does not read, so the engine has no filed capex value (last_filed_value null).

moat_against: No network effects or lock-in: leases roll (short shop leases), grocer anchors are powerful counterparties who can relocate or extract concessions at renewal, and anchor consolidation/bankruptcy is a recurring sector hit

Local scarcity is contestable: rival REITs (Kimco, Brixmor, Federal Realty) and private developers can build or redevelop competing centers; the moat is a portfolio of local positions, not a franchise

Rate and cap-rate exposure dominates: bond-like earnings, a guided 100-150bp refinancing drag as maturing debt reprices (search results), and a valuation multiple that compresses when rates rise regardless of operations

Growth is increasingly bought with capital: revenue CAGR is flattered by the all-stock Urstadt Biddle acquisition (closed Aug 18, 2023; +79 properties) and a development ramp from $232.9M (2023) to $435.1M (2025) of annual spend that depresses current owner's earnings; guided per-share growth is ~5% — utility-like
Discretionary tenant tail (restaurants, fitness, services) and geographic concentration — California and Florida together are roughly half of annual base rent (search results)
moat_for: Grocery-anchored necessity tenancy: >85% of centers grocery-anchored (search results), anchors 98.4% leased — weekly-trip tenancy that is e-commerce-resistant and feeds the shop tenants

Location scarcity in affluent suburbs: ~$150k average household income within 3 miles (search results), premier suburban trade areas where zoning constrains new competing supply; portfolio 96.9% leased / 94.5% commenced with a $41.2M signed-not-occupied rent pipeline (Q2 2026 release)

Demonstrated pricing power: blended cash rent spreads +10.4% in Q2 2026 (+11.8% trailing twelve months), straight-line +19.5%; same-property NOI +5.3% in 2025, guided +3.7-4.1% in 2026; annual escalators in most new leases (search results)

Development platform: $680M in-process at a ~9% blended estimated yield (Q2 2026 release) — building at yields well above acquisition cap rates, funded cheaply by an A-rated balance sheet (pro-rata net debt + preferred / EBITDAre 5.0x; 87.3% of consolidated real estate assets unencumbered, FY2025 10-K)
Returns corroborate a narrow moat: roic_proxy 7.3% / 8.5% / 9.3% / 7.7% in 2022-2025 (fundamentals.json), operating margin ~72% — above a REIT's cost of capital through the cycle so far
moat_justification: Moderate/narrow: grocery-anchored necessity centers in affluent, supply-constrained suburbs with demonstrated pricing power (Q2 2026 blended cash rent spreads +10.4%, same-property NOI guided +3.7-4.1% for 2026 after +5.3% in 2025) and a development platform building at ~9% yields — but no network effects or lock-in (leases roll, grocer anchors are powerful counterparties), each center's local position is contestable by rival REITs and developers, returns are rate/cap-rate dominated, and the measured returns corroborate only a narrow moat: roic_proxy 7.3% / 8.5% / 9.3% / 7.7% across 2022-2025 (fundamentals.json) — above a REIT cost of capital, not wide-moat territory, and flattered by a depreciated-cost asset denominator.
name: Regency Centers Corporation
one_liner: Premier grocery-anchored shopping-center REIT, moat 5/10 — but at $73.24 the TTM owner's-earnings yield is only 2.73% (base OE $2.00/share after charging all $435.1M of development & capital-improvement spend), so the weighted IRR is 6.25% with IV@15% of $20.78 and even the super-bull case earns just 9.76%; it clears the 15% hurdle only below ~$21. The REIT lens is kinder (FY2026 guided Nareit FFO $4.84–4.88/share, Core Operating Earnings $4.62–4.66/share), but no reading of the filed numbers supports a 15% owner's-earnings return at this price.
sector: Real Estate / REIT — Grocery-anchored shopping centers

shares_override.reason: DATA_GAP:shares — diluted weighted shares missing for FY2023, 2024, 2025 in companyfacts; only non-diluted outstanding counts are filed there. The filer's own FY2025 diluted weighted average count fills the gap; the engine applies this single value to every missing period (including the 2016/2021/2022 fallback history years, where it modestly understates OE/share vs the ~171M shares then outstanding — history only, not the base). The 3-yr median base is barely affected: FY2024's true diluted count (183,040,000) differs from the override by 0.4%. ttm.py uses the override unprorated as the TTM denominator — the current-period figure.
shares_override.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-13), Note 14 Earnings per Share and Unit, 'Parent Company Earnings per Share' table (in thousands, except per share data): weighted average common shares outstanding for diluted EPS 182,234 in 2025 (183,040 in 2024; 176,371 in 2023); diluted EPS $2.82 / $2.11 / $2.04 on net income attributable to common shareholders of $513,810 / $386,738 / $359,500 thousand. EDGAR companyfacts carries no weighted-average share series for CIK 910606 after FY2020 (the filer tags share counts with dimensions the aggregated facts drop), so the engine fell back to point-in-time CommonStockSharesOutstanding counts (184,581,070 / 181,361,454 / 182,902,234).
